title: The 10 Best Corded Table Saws
subtitle: Portable jobsite and benchtop table saws that plug in, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: We ranked 10 corded jobsite and benchtop table saws from Amazon's table saw best-sellers on rating, review volume, and features: an included stand, a rack and pinion fence, dado capability, and soft start. They run from a $180 benchtop saw to $649 for the Bosch GTS15-10, with either a 10-inch blade or the more portable 8-1/4-inch size.

changelog.note: Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on every listing. Price changes were all under 8%. Prices were captured during Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale, so some may be temporarily lower.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 10-Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Foldable Rolling Stand, 15 Amp, 32-1/2-Inch Rip Capacity (DWE7491RS)
products.verdict: The most-reviewed 10-inch jobsite saw on Amazon and the widest rip on this list at 32-1/2 inches, enough to split a 4x8 sheet down the middle. It comes on a folding rolling stand and is sold and shipped by Amazon.
pros: 32-1/2" rip capacity with a telescoping rack and pinion fence
Rolling stand included; folds down for the truck
3-1/8" depth of cut at 90 degrees, 2-1/4" at 45
Onboard storage for the guard, fence, riving knife, miter gauge, and wrenches
3-year limited warranty
cons: At 110 lb listed with the stand, it's the heaviest saw here
The included blade is a 24-tooth ripping blade; plan on a finer blade for plywood
The listing doesn't mention a dado insert or soft start

products.name: SKIL 15 Amp 10-Inch Jobsite Table Saw with Folding Stand (TS6307-00)
products.verdict: Amazon's #1 table saw right now: a 10-inch saw with rack and pinion fence rails and legs that fold into the body, for about half the price of the DEWALT. The rip is 7 inches shorter.
pros: Rack and pinion fence rails keep the fence parallel to the blade
Integrated folding legs, so no separate stand to buy
Takes an 8" dado stack up to 5/8" wide (dado insert sold separately)
Cuts a 4x4 in one pass at 90 degrees
3-year limited warranty; sold and shipped by Amazon
cons: 25-1/2" rip is short of the DEWALT's 32-1/2"
The listing doesn't say it has soft start
At $299 it sits right at our $300 budget line

products.name: DEWALT 15 Amp 8-1/4 in. Compact Portable Jobsite Table Saw (DWE7485)
products.verdict: The highest-rated saw on the list (4.8 stars across 5,814 reviews). The 8-1/4-inch blade trades cut depth for a 54 lb saw that one person can carry, and it still rips 24-1/2 inches.
pros: 4.8 stars from over 5,800 reviews
Rack and pinion telescoping fence rails
Metal roll cage and onboard storage for fence, guard, and miter gauge
Power-loss reset stops a surprise restart after an outage
cons: 8-1/4" blade means less depth of cut than a 10" saw
No stand in the box (see the DWE7485WS if you want one)
The listing doesn't mention a dado capacity

products.name: DEWALT Portable Table Saw with Stand, 8-1/4 inch, up to 48-Degree Angle Cuts (DWE7485WS)
products.verdict: The same DWE7485 saw bundled with DEWALT's jobsite stand for $20 more than the bare saw. If you don't already have a stand or a bench to bolt it to, this is the better buy of the two.
pros: Stand included for $20 over the saw alone
Rack and pinion telescoping fence rails, 24-1/2" rip
Blade brake and power-loss reset
Sold and shipped by Amazon

The listing's spec table says 4,300 rpm while its description says 5,800; the saw is the same DWE7485 listed at 5,800

products.name: SKILSAW 10 Inch Heavy Duty Worm Drive Table Saw with Stand (SPT99-11)
products.verdict: A worm-drive saw built for framing crews: the deepest cut here at 3-5/8 inches, a 30-1/2-inch rip, and a rolling stand with 16-inch wheels for rough ground.
pros: Deepest cut on the list: 3-5/8" at 90 degrees
Worm-drive gearing for torque in thick, wet, or treated lumber

products.name: BOSCH GTS15-10 10 Inch Portable Jobsite Table Saw with Gravity-Rise Wheeled Stand
products.verdict: The most complete feature set here: soft start, electronic speed regulation under load, a blade brake that stops in about three seconds, and Bosch's gravity-rise wheeled stand. It costs the most, and it has far fewer reviews than the DEWALT.
pros: Soft start reduces breaker trips on shared jobsite circuits
Brake stops the blade in about 3 seconds
Speed is electronically held under load
32-1/8" rip with a rack and pinion fence and color-coded index pins
Gravity-rise wheeled stand sets up and folds in one motion
cons: $649, the top price on the list

1-year limited warranty per the listing

avoid.name: VEVOR Table Saw with Stand, 10-inch 15-Amp, 25-in Max Rip Capacity, Cutting Speed up to 5000RPM, 40T Blade
avoid.flag: Spec table says 240 V; "-60 to 60 degree bevel" is the miter gauge range
avoid.verdict: The listing contradicts itself on voltage and on how far the blade tilts, and it has no model number. For less money, the SKIL TS6308 has a rack and pinion fence and a brand behind it.
reasons: The spec table lists 240 volts. The description says 120V/60Hz. Voltage is the one spec you can't get wrong on a saw you plug into a wall.

A bullet says you can set the blade anywhere from -60 to 60 degrees for bevel cuts. The description's own spec list shows -60 to +60 is the miter gauge range, and gives bevel depth only at 45 degrees.
The model number field just reads "Table Saw with Stand", so there's no model to look up for a manual, parts, or a replacement fence.
It's sold by a third-party storefront (VEMIXO) and the listing states no warranty term, only "limited warranty".

buyers_guide.a: A 10-inch saw cuts about 3 to 3-5/8 inches deep, enough for a 4x4 in one pass, and 10-inch blades are sold everywhere. An 8-1/4-inch saw cuts about 2-1/2 inches deep, which still handles 2x lumber and sheet goods, and weighs 40 to 55 lb. Buy the smaller saw if you carry it up stairs or between jobs often.

It's the widest board you can cut with the fence on the right side of the blade. At 24 inches or more you can split a 4x8 sheet of plywood down the middle. At 30 inches or more you can take a 2-foot shelf off the long edge of a sheet. Cheap benchtop saws often don't publish this number at all.

buyers_guide.q: Why does a rack and pinion fence matter?
buyers_guide.a: A rack and pinion fence moves both ends together on geared rails, so it stays parallel to the blade when you slide it. A cheaper clamp-on fence can lock slightly out of square, which makes the board pinch the blade and kick back. If you plan to rip much sheet stock, don't skip this feature.

A jobsite saw needs to sit at about waist height on something that won't move. Several saws here come on a folding or rolling stand. The compact 8-1/4-inch DEWALT DWE7485 and SKIL TS6308 don't, so either budget for a stand or bolt the saw to a sturdy bench.

buyers_guide.q: Can a portable table saw cut dados?
buyers_guide.a: Some can. You need a saw whose arbor and throat accept a stacked dado blade, plus a dado insert plate. Of the saws here, the Evolution R10TBLX ships with a dado plate, and the SKIL TS6307 takes an 8-inch dado stack up to 5/8 inch wide with an insert sold separately. Check the manual before buying a dado set for any saw.

buyers_guide.q: Will a 15-amp saw trip my breaker?
buyers_guide.a: Every saw here draws 15 amps, the full rating of a standard household circuit. Run it alone on the circuit, keep extension cords short and heavy-gauge, and consider a saw with soft start, like the Bosch GTS15-10 or Evolution R10TBLX, which ramps the motor up instead of hitting the circuit with a start-up spike.
